step.name: Step 1: Get Medical Attention Immediately
step.text: Your health is the absolute priority. Even if you feel okay at the scene, some injuries can have delayed symptoms. See a doctor as soon as possible to get thoroughly checked out. This not only protects your health but also creates an official record of your injuries, which is vital for any future claim.

step.name: Step 2: Document Everything at the Scene
step.text: If you're able, gather as much information as you can. Take photos of the vehicles, the accident scene, road conditions, and any visible injuries. Get contact information from witnesses and the other driver, and note down police report numbers. This detailed evidence will be incredibly helpful later.

step.name: Step 3: Be Cautious with Insurance Companies
step.text: The other driver's insurance company might contact you quickly. Remember, their goal is to pay out as little as possible. Avoid giving recorded statements or signing anything until you've spoken with someone who can represent your interests. You don't have to tell them everything right away.

step.name: Step 4: Understand Your Rights and Options
step.text: This is where things can get really complicated. Understanding what you're entitled to—like compensation for medical bills, lost wages, and pain and suffering—and navigating California law requires expertise. Don't try to figure it all out alone.

step.name: Step 5: Seek Professional Legal Guidance
step.text: An experienced personal injury attorney, especially one familiar with car accidents in San Diego, can be a game-changer. They can handle all communications with insurance companies, investigate your claim thoroughly, gather necessary evidence, and negotiate for the best possible outcome. They ensure your concerns are heard and your strategy is tailored to your unique situation, giving you the best chance for fair compensation. Don't hesitate to reach out for a free consultation to understand your legal standing.
